instrument_name: Healthy Workplaces Act, Laws 2021 ch. 131 (HB 20, final passed text), codified NMSA 1978 50-17-1 to 50-17-12
figure_or_rule_carried: Private employers with 1+ employees (excludes US, state, political subdivisions; railway-labor employees excluded). Accrual min 1 hour per 30 hours worked from start of employment, or frontload 64 h on 1 January (pro rata for later hires); use cap 64 h per 12-month period; unused leave carries over; no payout at separation (3(B)(4)); reinstated if rehired within 12 months; FLSA 213(a)(1) exempt staff assumed 40 h/week; paid at the same hourly rate and benefits, not below minimum wage (2(C)); notice at hire in English, Spanish or language of the majority; records of hours and sick leave kept 48 months (6). Effective 2022-07-01 (s.13). Codification numbers per NM compilation, not read on the compilation itself.

instrument_name: 11.1.6 NMAC Healthy Workplaces (DWS Labor Relations Division rule)
authority: NM State Records Center and Archives (NMAC) / NM DWS Labor Relations Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Confirms codification of the Healthy Workplaces Act at NMSA 50-17-1 to 50-17-12 (authority 50-17-9). Frontloaded leave may not be recouped by payroll deduction even with written authorization or on separation (8A); hours over 40/week accrue at 1:30 unless higher rate chosen (8B); ESL paid for regularly scheduled hours, fluctuating schedules = average of preceding two weeks (8C); ESL paid on the same scheduled payday as regular wages (8E); records 48 months (8F); year-to-date written summary of ESL accrued and used at least once per calendar quarter, may be electronic or on the earnings statement (8G).

instrument_name: 11.1.4 NMAC Wage and Hour and Employment of Children (DWS Labor Relations Division rule)
authority: NM State Records Center and Archives (NMAC) / NM DWS Labor Relations Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Implements NMSA ch. 50 arts 1, 4, 6. Wages (50-4-1) include vacation pay and other pay for time not worked where it is compensation under the employer's written policy (7O). Written authorization (signed at hire or before the deduction) needed to deduct an advance or overpayment, and the employee must still receive at least minimum wage x hours worked (7R). Work permit ordinarily required for children under 16 (9). Supervisor exemption test for 50-4-1(C)(2) (7F).

instrument_name: Laws 2019 ch. 30 (SB 437, final passed text) amending Minimum Wage Act NMSA 50-4-21 and 50-4-22
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 12.00 USD/h on and after 2023-01-01 (no automatic indexation in the text); secondary-school students after school/when school is out 8.50/h from 2020-01-01; tipped employees (>30 USD/month in tips) cash wage 3.00/h from 2023-01-01, tips + cash must reach 12.00, tip pooling among wait staff allowed; agricultural employers may deduct reasonable value of food, utilities, supplies, housing; overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 h in a 7-day week (50-4-22(E)). 'Employee' excludes domestic service in a private home, bona fide executive/administrative/professional and supervisors, federal employees, commission/piecework salespersons, registered apprentices, under-18 non-students, G.I. trainees, certified seasonal camp staff, specified agricultural employees, agricultural-commodity processors, residential nonprofit staff; state and political subdivisions are covered for the minimum-wage rate (50-4-22(A)) only. 2020-2022 steps 9.00/10.50/11.50 (historic).

instrument_name: NM DWS Labor Relations - Minimum Wage Information page (Wayback capture 2026-06-15)
authority: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, Labor Relations Division
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum 12.00/h effective 2023-01-01 (11.50 from 2022-01-01); tipped 3.00/h effective 2023-01-01; 'the state will enforce the highest available rate'; lists local ordinances: Albuquerque, Bernalillo County, Las Cruces, City of Santa Fe, Santa Fe County. No 2026/2027 state change shown in the June 2026 capture (consistent with SB 437 having no indexation).

instrument_name: City of Albuquerque - Albuquerque Minimum Wage Information (2027 adjustment)
figure_or_rule_carried: Albuquerque minimum wage 12.00/h for 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31); 13.00/h from 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31 (+1.00, 8.3%); 12.00/h in 2027 where the employer provides healthcare and/or childcare benefits costing at least 2,500 USD annualized; tipped employee cash wage 7.20/h (55% of the 2027 minimum) for 2026 and 2027. Ordinance and rules PDFs linked, not read.

instrument_name: City of Santa Fe - Living Wage in the City of Santa Fe (2026 rate and 2027 amendment)
authority: City of Santa Fe, Office of Economic Development
article_or_section: Current Living Wage; 2026 calculation; amendment summary
figure_or_rule_carried: Living wage 15.40/h from 2026-03-01 for all employers within city limits (15.00 from 2025); one-time increase to 17.50/h from 2027-01-01; from 2028-03-01 annual adjustment 50% Western CPI + 50% HUD 2-bedroom FMR, capped at 5%, never decreased. Tipped/commissioned employees earning >=100 USD/month: base 3.00/h with tips topping up to 15.40. G-DERIVE: 15.00 x 1.0268 (Western Region CPI-W 12-month increase per the page) = 15.402 -> 15.40. Ordinance number of the 2027 amendment not read on the page.

instrument_name: NM DWS How UI Tax Rates Are Calculated (Wayback 2026-06-14) - experience-rating and wage-file details
authority: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, UI Tax
article_or_section: Experienced Employers; Excess Claims Premium; Rate Calculation and Definitions; Wage File Formats
figure_or_rule_carried: Rate = benefit ratio x reserve factor x experience history factor x 100 (HB 283, from 2016-07-01); reserve factor 0.5-4.0, 2026 = 3.6361 (2025 = 3.5719, per UI Tax page US-NM-P5-1-001); experience history factor 0.40-1.00 by employer reserve band; contribution rate floor 0.33% and cap 5.4% (NMSA 51-1-11 per page); excess claims premium = (pre-cap rate - 5.4%) x 10%, max 1% of taxable payroll; computation date 30 June; quarterly Employment and Wage Detail Report; wage file formats published: Delimited, ICESA, XML, EFW2 (specifications linked, not read). Complements US-NM-P5-1-002 (same file).

instrument_name: 11.1.2 NMAC Public Works Minimum Wage Act rule - certified payroll provisions
authority: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, Labor Relations Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Contracts over 60,000 USD (see US-NMP6-002): contractors and all subcontractor tiers submit certified weekly payroll records bi-weekly to the prime contractor and contracting agency within 5 working days after the close of the second payroll period, and to the director on request; payroll content: name and address (first payroll), classification, hourly wage and fringe rates, overtime rate, daily and weekly hours per classification incl. actual overtime, itemized deductions, net wages, wage-rate decision number; payrolls numbered sequentially; bi-weekly statement of compliance; affidavit before final payment; records kept at least 4 years after contract completion. Apprentices must be registered.

instrument_name: New Mexico New Hire Directory - Law and Reporting Fundamentals pages
authority: New Mexico New Hire Directory (state directory operated for NM; HCA Child Support Services)
article_or_section: Law (NMSA 50-13-1 to 50-13-4; 42 USC 653a); What/When to report
figure_or_rule_carried: Report new hires and rehires (return after 60+ days separation/leave without pay) who reside or work in NM within 20 days of hire; electronic/magnetic reporters: two monthly transmissions not more than 16 days apart. Required: employer FEIN (same FEIN as quarterly wage report), name, payroll address; employee name, mailing address, SSN, date of hire. Optional: employer phone/fax/email/contact; employee state of hire, date of birth. Penalty up to 20 USD per unreported hire, 500 USD on conspiracy. Online/file transfer at nm-newhire.com. Multistate employers may designate one state (federal rule). Child support payments: NM CSSD State Disbursement Unit, P.O. Box 200796, Dallas TX 75320-0796.

instrument_name: NM TRD Instructions for TRD-41414 Wage Withholding Tax Return
authority: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
article_or_section: Filing Periods and Due Dates; Line Instructions; Penalty and Interest
figure_or_rule_carried: TRD-41414 (replaced CRS-1 from 2021-07-01) is the wage withholding return; filing status monthly, quarterly or semiannual as shown on the registration certificate issued by TRD (no dollar thresholds stated in the instructions); due on or before the 25th of the month after the period (monthly: e.g. Feb -> Mar 25; semiannual Jul-Dec -> Jan 25); weekend/holiday -> next business day; seasonal/temporary/special-event filers use monthly status; amended return carries full corrected amounts; e-file mandate with waiver (RPD-41351) / exception (RPD-41350) forms; interest at IRC individual rate, none if under 1 USD; returned check penalty 20 USD; late penalty up to 20%. A zero return is required when no tax is due (FYI-104).

instrument_name: NM TRD E-file and E-pay Mandate, effective 2026-01-01 (Section 9-11-6.4 NMSA 1978)
authority: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
figure_or_rule_carried: For filing periods from 2026-01-01 TRD mandates electronic filing and payment of TRD-41431 (Workers' Compensation Fee Return and Employees' Quarterly Wage and Withholding Report, due the 25th after quarter end; new return format, bulk-filing schema, ACH credit), TRD-41414 (refund claim on return, new bulk-filing schema) and TRD-41409. Bulk filer schema in TAP (Help > FAQ > Bulk), announced mid-January 2026 - not obtained. Payment methods: credit card, ACH debit (TAP EFT), ACH credit, Fedwire (FYI-401). WKC ACH credit addendum uses FEIN, tax type 020, e.g. TXP*777777777*020*20260331*T*9999 (with trailing backslash). WKC fee per employee 4.80 from 2025-07-01 (employer 2.55 + employee 2.25; SB 535).

instrument_name: NM TRD Withholding Tax and Workers' Compensation page (live, read 2026-11-02)
authority: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
article_or_section: Registration; Who Must Withhold; Reporting Tax Withheld; Workers' Compensation
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers must register with TRD to file; definitions of employer, employee, wages in 7-3-3 NMSA 1978; exceptions: certain nonresidents, active-duty military pay, income wholly earned by an enrolled Native American member on the lands of the nation/tribe/pueblo where enrolled and living; WC fee schedule 2.30/2.55/2.68/2.80 employer and 2.00/2.25/2.38/2.50 employee (52-5-19). Page still says information returns are 'generally' due by the last day of February - conflicts with FYI-330 Rev. 12/2025 (31 January for W-2/W-2G/1099-R from 2026); build follows FYI-330.

instrument_name: NM 2017 Senate Bill 109 (introduced, 53rd Legislature) reprinting NMSA 50-4-4, 50-4-5 and 50-4-7 as then in force
figure_or_rule_carried: Bill text reprints law then in force (bracketed words = proposed deletions, gender-neutral style only). 50-4-4(A): on discharge, fixed and definite wages are due immediately on demand and must be paid within 5 days of discharge; (B) task/piece/commission or other calculated pay within 10 days; (C) wages continue at the same rate from discharge until paid (waiting-time), only if demand was made and refused, capped at the 60th day after discharge. 50-4-5: employee without a written contract for a definite period who quits or resigns is paid at the next succeeding payday (employer may pay immediately). 50-4-7: in a dispute the employer gives written notice of and pays unconditionally the amount conceded due within the 50-4-4/50-4-5 times. Later amendments not excluded (compilation not readable: nmlegis.gov and nmonesource.com 403).

instrument_name: NM 2023 SB 216 (final passed text) amending NMSA 35-12-7 garnishment exemptions and 35-12-18 writ form
figure_or_rule_carried: Creditor garnishment (other than child support): exempt is the GREATER of 75% of disposable earnings per pay period or, per week, 40 x the highest applicable federal, state or local minimum hourly wage at the place the wages were earned (state 12.00 -> 480/week; Albuquerque 2027 13.00 -> 520; Santa Fe 15.40 -> 616); RLD Financial Institutions Division publishes the equivalent table for other pay periods; child-support garnishment: 50% of disposable earnings exempt, and garnishment + wage deduction for child support together max 50%; disposable earnings = wages after deductions required by law; exempt amounts stay exempt in a bank account if traceable. Writs issued in advance of judgment do not attach wages. Applies to actions filed on or after 2023-07-01. 'final' = text as passed by both chambers; governor's signature/chapter number not read (confidence medium-high that it is law).

instrument_name: NM DWS Unemployment Insurance Employer Handbook (2019 edition, Wayback copy)
authority: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions
article_or_section: Financing; Tax Liability; Non-covered Employment; Reportable Wages; Quarterly reports; Taxable Wage Base; Business Transfers
figure_or_rule_carried: No employee UI contribution: employers may not deduct UI tax from wages. Liability: non-agricultural payroll >= 450 USD in a quarter or 1+ worker in 20 weeks; agricultural >= 20,000 USD in a quarter or 10+ workers in 20 weeks; domestic >= 1,000 USD in a quarter. Exempt employers NMSA 51-1-42(E); exempt wages 51-1-42(F); 501(c)(3) may elect reimbursement (payments in lieu due 30 days after quarter). Quarterly wage and contribution report due last day of the month after quarter end, electronic only, zero report required, wages reported when paid; interest 1%/month on late contributions. Wages in lieu of notice and pay in lieu of dismissal are reportable wages; severance/voluntary buyout and legal settlements are not. Taxable wage base indexed = 60% of state average annual earnings of the second preceding year, rounded up to next 100 USD (2026 = 34,800 per US-NM-P5-1-001). Successor must apply for experience transfer before its first quarterly report due date (50 USD penalty). 2019 edition: figures other than the rules above must come from the 2026 pages.
